column1: NURSING 4403A - ADV HEALTH ASSESSMNT & DIAG I
column2: Course Description: Concepts and frameworks integral to advanced health assessment and diagnosis in nursing practice are introduced Comprehensive and focused health assessment, including history taking, physical assessment and diagnostic reasoning as well as laboratory and diagnostic test selection and interpretation for the adult client are emphasized, laying the foundation for clinical decision-making from data collection to diagnostic plan of care. Extra Information: 3 theory hours and 3 practice hours, term one.

column1: NURSING 4404B - ADV HEALTH ASSESSMNT & DIAG II
column2: Course Description: This course builds on applies the skills and frameworks, concepts and methods of health assessment and clinical decision-making studied in AHAD I to specific populations across the lifespan, to families and to the community. Advanced practice skill pertaining to diagnostic test assessment is examined. Extra Information: 3 theory hours and 3 practice hours, term two.

column1: NURSING 4405A - THERPEUTCS PRIMRY HLTH CARE I
column2: Course Description: Concepts integral to pharmacoltherapy, advanced counselling and complimentary therapies related predominantly to common episodic conditions of clients across the lifespan are introduced. Emphasis is on the therapeutic care plan approach which focuses on drug-related problems, goals of therapies, analysis of different therapeutic approaches, need for referral, monitoring parameters, acceptability to the client, and follow-up. Extra Information: 3 theory hours and 3 practice hours, term one.

column1: NURSING 4406B - THERPEUTCS PRIMRY HLTH CARE II
column2: Course Description: This course builds on the knowledge acquired in AHAD I and Therapeutics I and applies the frameworks and concepts of pharmacotherapy, advanced counselling, and complimentary therapies predominantly to clients with chronic conditions and special populations. Extra Information: 3 theory hours and 3 practice hours, term two.

Course Description: A systems approach is used to examine concepts in pathophysiology as a basis for advanced nursing practice. A case study approach provides a comprehensive overview of the etiology, pathogenesis, and clinical manifestations of diseases in adults and children. Builds upon knowledge of normal anatomy and physiology across the lifespan. Extra Information: 3 hours.

Course Description: Examination of the roles and responsibilities of the primary care nurse practitioner, historical development, relationships with clients and other health providers, legal and ethical issues, scope of practice and functioning in interdisciplinary teams, primary health policy formulation and political strategies are addressed. Extra Information: 3 hours.

Course Description: Explore the fundamental principles and practices of perioperative nursing. Students will learn to scrub, gown, glove, and mask using strict aseptic technique. Lab practice will include draping and skin preparation. Students will be introduced to the selection and use of surgical instruments, supplies, and equipment used in the surgical suite.Antirequisite(s): Nursing 4140W/X from 2013-14 to 2015-16.
